G-01.title: Earth Fact Sheet
G-01.note: Earth mass, radius, sidereal day 23.9345 h, obliquity 23.44 deg, escape velocity 11.186 km/s, mean orbital velocity 29.78 km/s, orbit period.

G-02.title: Moon Fact Sheet
G-02.note: Moon mass ratio 0.0123, semimajor axis 384.4e3 km, sidereal period 27.3217 d, inclination 5.145 deg, mean orbital velocity 1.022 km/s.

G-03.title: Sun Fact Sheet
G-03.note: Sun mass 1.9884e30 kg (332,900 Earth masses), mean radius 695,700 km, obliquity 7.25 deg, rotation 609.12 h at 16 deg latitude.

G-04.title: Planetary Fact Sheet - Metric (comparison table)
G-04.note: Rotation periods, orbital velocities, escape velocities, orbital periods, mean temperatures of all planets.

G-05.title: Mercury Fact Sheet
G-05.note: Mercury mass, radius, rotation 1407.6 h, obliquity 0.034 deg.

G-06.title: Venus Fact Sheet
G-06.note: Venus mass, radius, retrograde rotation -5832.6 h, obliquity 177.36 deg, orbit period 224.701 d, synodic period 583.92 d, 464 C.

G-07.title: Mars Fact Sheet
G-07.note: Mars mass, radius, orbit period 686.980 d, semimajor axis 227.956e6 km, obliquity 25.19 deg.

G-08.title: Jupiter Fact Sheet
G-08.note: Jupiter mass 1898.13e24 kg, radius 69,911 km, rotation 9.925 h, semimajor axis 5.2034 AU.

G-09.title: Saturn Fact Sheet
G-09.note: Saturn mass, radius, mean density 687 kg/m3 (less than water), rotation 10.656 h.

G-10.title: Uranus Fact Sheet
G-10.note: Uranus mass, radius, obliquity 97.77 deg, retrograde rotation.

G-11.title: Neptune Fact Sheet
G-11.note: Neptune mass, radius, obliquity 28.32 deg, wind speeds 0-580 m/s.

G-12.title: Pluto Fact Sheet
G-12.note: Pluto mass 0.01303e24 kg, radius 1188 km, obliquity 119.51 deg, retrograde rotation.

G-13.title: Approximate Positions of the Planets (Keplerian elements, Table 1, 1800-2050 AD)
G-13.note: Standish and Williams J2000 mean elements (a, e, I, L, long. peri, long. node) used by the app for the eight planets.

G-14.title: Astrodynamic Parameters
G-14.note: AU = 149,597,870,700 m, GM_Sun = 1.32712440041e20 m3/s2, G, c, GM Earth, GM Moon (Earth/Moon mass ratio 81.30).

G-15.title: CODATA recommended value: Newtonian constant of gravitation

G-16.title: IAU 2015 Resolution B3 on nominal conversion constants for selected solar and planetary properties (arXiv:1510.07674)
G-16.note: Defines nominal solar radius and nominal solar mass parameter as exact values; numerical values are quoted in G-03 (radius) and G-14 (GM).

G-17.title: Voyager 1
G-17.note: Launch 5 Sep 1977, Jupiter 5 Mar 1979, Saturn 12 Nov 1980, exit of heliosphere 25 Aug 2012, climb out of the ecliptic after Saturn.

G-18.title: Voyager 2
G-18.note: Launch 20 Aug 1977, Jupiter 9 Jul 1979, Saturn 25 Aug 1981, Uranus 24 Jan 1986, Neptune 25 Aug 1989.

G-19.title: Voyager mission overview
G-19.note: Voyager 1 reached the interstellar boundary in 2012, Voyager 2 in 2018; both leave at more than 3 AU per year.

G-20.title: The Grand Tour
G-20.note: Voyager used a once-every-175-year alignment of the outer planets; gravity assists chain Jupiter to Neptune.

G-21.title: Oort Cloud and Scale of the Solar System (infographic)
G-21.note: Voyager 2 termination shock at 84 AU (Aug 2007), Voyager 2 about 119 AU, Oort Cloud from about 1,000 AU to about 100,000 AU.

G-22.title: Webb Orbit
G-22.note: Sun-Earth L1 and L2 about 1.5 million km from Earth; L1-L3 metastable, L4/L5 stable; SOHO, DSCOVR at L1; Webb orbits L2 in about 6 months; asteroids at L4/L5.

G-23.title: WMAP overview (Sun-Earth Lagrange points diagram)
G-23.note: L2 is 1.5 million km from Earth; geometry of L1-L5; WMAP, Planck, Webb at L2.

G-24.title: Euclid fact sheet
G-24.note: Euclid at Sun-Earth L2, 1.5 million km from Earth, large Lissajous/halo orbit of about 1 million km.

G-25.title: Vigil mission overview
G-25.note: Vigil to orbit Sun-Earth L5, launch planned 2031 on Ariane 6.

G-26.title: Newly discovered asteroid just second of its kind (2020 XL5)
G-26.note: 2020 XL5 confirmed as the second known Earth Trojan (after 2010 TK7); published Feb 2022.

G-27.title: GW150914
G-27.note: Detection on 14 Sep 2015, source about 1.3 billion light-years away.

G-28.title: Gravitational-wave science
G-28.note: GW150914 observed Sep 2015, reported Feb 2016; typical arm-length oscillations ten thousand times smaller than a proton.

G-29.title: Astronomers reveal first image of the black hole at the heart of our galaxy (eso2208)
G-29.note: Sgr A* mass about 4 million solar masses, released 12 May 2022, EHT 2017 observations, Genzel and Ghez star-orbit work.

G-30.title: Detection of the gravitational redshift in the orbit of the star S2 near the Galactic centre massive black hole (abstract)
G-30.note: S2 has a 16-year orbit and about 7650 km/s at pericentre.

G-31.title: Perihelion Precessions of Inner Planets in Einstein's Theory and Predicted Values for the Cosmological Constant
G-31.note: GR contribution to Mercury perihelion precession 42.9815 arcsec per century; observed unexplained advance 42.980 +/- 0.002 arcsec per century.

G-32.title: Sun's Gravity Bends Starlight (Cosmic Times, 1919)
G-32.note: Eddington's 1919 eclipse expedition found the bending predicted by general relativity; caveat on sensitivity of the 1919 data.

G-33.title: Sun: Facts
G-33.note: Galactic orbit about 230 million years at 720,000 km/h; Sun is 99.8% of system mass; formed about 4.6 billion years ago.

G-34.title: Solar System: Facts
G-34.note: Orbital speed around the galaxy about 828,000 km/h (230 km/s); galactic year about 230 million years; age 4.6 billion years.

G-35.title: Magnetospheres (focus area)
G-35.note: Dayside magnetosphere 6-10 Earth radii; magnetotail hundreds of Earth radii, past the Moon at 60; field from convecting molten iron.

G-36.title: Ulysses Begins to Explore Sun's Northern Pole
G-36.note: Solar wind about 400 km/s near the equator and 800 km/s at high latitude; about 1 million tons per second lost.

G-37.title: 100 Years of General Relativity (Blueshift)
G-37.note: GPS clocks: -7 microseconds/day (special relativity), +45 (general relativity), net +38 microseconds/day, about 10 km/day error if uncorrected.

G-38.title: Geoid (GOCO06s model visualization)
G-38.note: Geoid ranges from +85 m (Iceland) to -106 m (south of India); visualization exaggerates by 10,000.

G-39.title: What Causes Tides?
G-39.note: Tidal force from the difference in the Moon's pull; two bulges; most coasts have two highs and two lows per day.

G-40.title: Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters (abstract)
G-40.note: Omega_c h2 = 0.120, Omega_b h2 = 0.0224 (dark matter about 5.4 times baryonic matter); H0 = 67.4. Age 13.80 Gyr is in the paper's parameter tables.

G-41.title: Planck 2018 results. I. Overview (dipole, ar5iv HTML)
G-41.note: Solar-system velocity relative to the CMB 369.82 +/- 0.11 km/s.

G-42.title: Dark Matter
G-42.note: Ordinary matter about 5% and dark matter about 27% of the universe (about 5.4 to 1); Rubin's outer-star speeds.

G-43.title: There's More to the North Star Than Meets the Eye

G-44.title: Why is Polaris the North Star? (StarChild)
G-44.note: Axial precession period about 26,000 years; Vega will be the North Star in about 13,000 years.

G-45.title: Orbits and Kepler's Laws
G-45.note: Statement of Kepler's three laws, p^2 = a^3; Mercury 88 d, Earth 365 d, Saturn 10,759 d.

G-46.title: Kepler's 3rd Law - Lesson Plan #31 (first cosmic velocity)
G-46.note: First cosmic velocity 7.9 km/s (circular orbit at 1 Earth radius); escape velocity 11.2 km/s = 7.9 x sqrt(2); no third cosmic velocity.

G-47.title: What Is a Barycenter?
G-47.note: Sun-Jupiter barycenter lies just outside the Sun's surface.

G-48.title: 2025 Exoplanet Archive News
G-48.note: Archive reached 6,000 confirmed planets on 17 Sep 2025.

G-49.title: First Close-up of the Far Side of Moon (Luna 3)
G-49.note: Luna 3 took the first images of the lunar far side on 7 Oct 1959 (29 photographs, about 70% coverage).

G-50.title: Galaxies and the Expanding Universe
G-50.note: Sun about 28,000 light-years from the galactic centre, roughly two-thirds of the way out; about 400 billion stars.

G-51.title: Galaxies
G-51.note: Solar system lies on a spiral arm about halfway from the galactic centre.

G-52.title: Pluto: Facts
G-52.note: Reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006; axis tilted 57 degrees to its orbit plane (equivalent to a retrograde obliquity of about 123 degrees).

G-53.title: NASA's WISE Finds Earth's First Trojan Asteroid
G-53.note: 2010 TK7 is the first Earth Trojan; Trojans share a planet's orbit near stable points ahead of or behind it.

G-55.title: 175 Years Ago: Astronomers Discover Neptune, the Eighth Planet
G-55.note: Neptune found on 23-24 Sep 1846 from a mathematically predicted position.

G-56.title: COBE science
G-56.note: CMB temperature varies by only 1 part in 100,000.

G-57.title: Major Groups of Dinosaurs
G-57.note: Earliest dinosaur fossils about 235 million years old (Late Triassic).

G-58.title: Then vs. Now: The Age of the Universe
G-58.note: WMAP-era age 13.7 +/- 0.2 billion years (superseded by Planck 13.80 +/- 0.02).
